turns.user: my squat's been stuck for a bit, what should I do
turns.reply:
When a squat gets stuck, it's usually one of three things holding it up: your bracing, your recovery, or just needing a fresh stimulus to spark some new adaptation. 

Since you've been hitting 45kg for 3x8 recently, the first thing to look at is how you're preparing for each rep. If you aren't actively pulling a massive breath into your abdomen and clamping your core down like you're about to get punched, you'll lose power at the bottom of the squat. 

If your bracing is already rock-solid, we can look at changing up the stimulus. One option is to temporarily swap the back squat for something like a goblet squat or a box squat to build confidence and power in a slightly different pattern, or we can adjust the volume on Tuesdays to let you recover better. 

How have those heavy sets of squats actually felt on your back and legs when you've hit that 8th rep?

turns.user: ok, and how long before I'd expect that to move
turns.reply:
If we dial in your bracing and keep your recovery on point, you should start seeing the bar speed improve within two to three weeks, with the actual weight on the bar moving up shortly after. 

If we swap the movement or adjust the volume to break the plateau, we usually give that new stimulus a full 4-week block to do its job. Strength adaptations take a little time to register in the tendons and nervous system, so patience is key. 

Are you noticing the struggle right out of the bottom of the squat, or are you getting stuck halfway up?
